name: The final sequence of the Kaivalya-pāda (YS 4.25–34)

stages.name: sattva-puruṣa-anyatā-khyāti
stages.gloss: cognition of the distinctness of sattva and puruṣa
stages.description: Overlordship and omniscience follow for one established only in this cognition (3.49); the yogin does not rest in them but goes on to dispassion towards them (3.50).

stages.name: tad-vairāgya, doṣa-bīja-kṣaya
stages.gloss: dispassion even towards that; destruction of the seeds of defect
stages.description: The seeds of affliction go to dissolution with the mind and puruṣa no longer undergoes the threefold suffering; kaivalya (3.50).

stages.name: ātmabhāva-bhāvanā-nivṛtti
stages.gloss: cessation of the cultivation of self-becoming
stages.description: For one who sees the distinction (4.25).

stages.name: viveka-nimna kaivalya-prāgbhāra citta
stages.gloss: mind inclined to discrimination, sloping towards kaivalya
stages.description: 4.26; other cognitions still arise in its gaps from earlier saṃskāras and their abandoning is like that of the afflictions (4.27-4.28).

stages.name: dharma-megha samādhi
stages.description: For one without desire even in prasaṃkhyāna, from discrimination-vision in every way (4.29).

stages.name: kleśa-karma-nivṛtti
stages.description: The knowing one is liberated even while living (bhāṣya 4.30); knowledge is endless and the knowable little (4.31).

stages.name: guṇānāṃ pariṇāma-krama-samāpti
stages.gloss: end of the sequence of the guṇas' transformations
stages.description: The guṇas, their purpose fulfilled, complete their sequence (4.32-4.33).

stages.name: kaivalya
stages.description: The return to source of the guṇas empty of puruṣa's purpose, or the establishment of the power of consciousness in its own form (4.34); also 3.55: sattva and puruṣa equal in purity.
